column2: ENGLISH

Your challenge has been issued and so it echoes across the plains: You will organise a great tournament to please Khorne and gain his favour. Any who believes they are worthy of the gaze of the Skull God will gather and you will fight all night and bleed and kill until only one remains to bask in the triumph of ultimate victory!
BLOOD FOR THE BLOOD GOD!

I challenge you, scum!
 I call upon you to shed blood in name of Khorne! Meet me and any others who will heed this call at the plains and face my wrath! Only the strongest will survive to bask in the glory of Lord of Skulls!!

 [From.GetTitledFirstName]
I'll rip your heart OUT!!
You're not worthy of my blade.

You miserable worm!
 Ready yourself to depart from this world! Before the next moon, the Bloodletters will feast upon your wretched soul as I claim my rightful place at Khorne's side!

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Ah!
The boasts of the weak do not concern me. \n Shriek and batter all you want, but that won't make you a worthy adversary to fell with my blade, [From.GetTitledFirstName]
Coward!

Several warriors have answered your call, gathering in the barren plain chosen for the deadly tournament in honour of the Lord of Skulls. Not all are challengers, the word of the great bloodbath caught the attention of many aspiring champions, wanderers, the curious and traders.\n Once you and the other challengers are gathered, all of the other followers surround you, looking towards you in anticipation.\n Above them, the tattered tabards with Khorne's rune blow in a hot wind, their poles already surrounded by little offerings.

Not enough warriors came at your call. The plain lies empty before you, with just some curious cultists roaming around, squabbling over minor quarrels. You've waited for a few days now and it is certain no one else will come.\n It is with great regret that you announce you are forced to cancel the tournament.
BLOOD! BLOOD AND SKULLS!!
This was a waste of time.

Not all are challengers, the word of the great bloodbath caught the attention of many aspiring champions, wanderers, the curious and traders.\n Once you and the other challengers are gathered, all of the other followers surround you, looking towards you in anticipation.\n Above them, the tattered tabards with Khorne's rune blow in a hot wind, their poles already surrounded by little offerings.
BLOOD! BLOOD AND SKULLS!!
As the first challenger, it is only right that you have the honour of starting the deathmatch. Khorne only favours the ruthless and the strong.
Glory to Khorne! Face me!

It is your turn to fight for the glory of Khorne and yourself. You walk towards the centre of the plain, accompanied by the cheering of the cultists sitting and standing in the field around you. [From.GetFirstName], your adversary, comes from the opposite side to meet you in the middle. You roar and beat your weapons on your armour, before charging each other.
DIE!!!

You charge [combatant_2.GetFirstName], smashing [combatant_2.GetHerHis] armor in with a powerful blow and preparing to cut off [combatant_2.GetHerHis] head with your blade as [combatant_2.GetSheHe] lies on the ground, but [combatant_2.GetFirstName] manages to dodge your attack, rolling on the side and tripping you with a kick. Your opponent gets back on [combatant_2.GetHerHis] feet, charging in, waving [combatant_2.GetHerHis] weapon towards you, but you manage to take advantage of [combatant_2.GetHerHis] recklessness and plunge your blade through [combatant_2.GetHerHis] neck.

[combatant_2.GetFirstName] draws the first blood, cutting a long red line on your arm with [combatant_2.GetHerHis] blade and pushing you away with [combatant_2.GetHerHis] shield before you could counterattack. Your opponent licks off the blood from [combatant_2.GetHerHis] weapon and charges again. You clash your blades several times, taunting and grunting, but, when you finally start to tire your arm, you manage to get an opening and cut through [combatant_2.GetHerHis] chest.

You ram into [combatant_2.GetFirstName], raising [combatant_2.GetHerHim] over your head and tossing [combatant_2.GetHerHim] away, then you run to recover your weapon while [combatant_2.GetSheHe] tries to get back on [combatant_2.GetHerHis] feet. \n Your opponent growls something, bashing [combatant_2.GetHerHis] blade on [combatant_2.GetHerHis] shield. When you reach [combatant_2.GetHerHim] [combatant_2.GetSheHe] swings the blade to chop your head off, but you're fast enough to drop on your knees and slice [combatant_2.GetHerHim] from belly to neck.

You exchange swings and blows with your adversary for what seems hours, each of you shouting insults to the other. [combatant_2.GetFirstName] finally manages to break the stall by feinting a thrust and then ramming on you with [combatant_2.GetHerHis] shoulder. You drag [combatant_2.GetHerHim] on the ground as well, starting to punch and bite [combatant_2.GetHerHim], until your teeth finally grab hold of [combatant_2.GetHerHis] neck and tear it open.

You start the duel confident of your abilities, but you soon realize your opponent is tougher than [combatant_2.GetSheHe] appears. [combatant_2.GetFirstName] quickly overcomes you, striking you down, dragging you by the neck for all to see, shouting [combatant_2.GetHerHis] victory.\n Your shame channels anger even more and you finally find the strength to free yourself of [combatant_2.GetHerHis] hold and start choking [combatant_2.GetHerHim]. [combatant_2.GetFirstName] struggles, but it is of no avail to [combatant_2.GetHerHim] and soon falls dead on the ground.

A timely charge allows you to push down your opponent at the start of the duel. You jump on [combatant_2.GetFirstName], painfully crushing [combatant_2.GetHerHis] knees and cutting a gash under [combatant_2.GetHerHis] arm.\n Your opponent screams, but [combatant_2.GetSheHe] will not admit defeat. Rolling on the side, [combatant_2.GetSheHe] throws [combatant_2.GetHerHis] weapon at you, striking you on the shoulder. Limping back on [combatant_2.GetHerHis] uninjured leg, [combatant_2.GetSheHe] tries to tackle you from below, but you're quicker to plunge your blade into [combatant_2.GetHerHis] spine.

Your last strike is so hard, you cut [combatant_2.GetFirstName]'s weapon in half. Shouting your imminent triumph, you advance as [combatant_2.GetSheHe] retreats.\n You need to accuse [combatant_2.GetHerHim] of cowardice several times before [combatant_2.GetSheHe] finally stops running and faces you again.\n Using [combatant_2.GetHerHis] arms to shield [combatant_2.GetHerHim]self, [combatant_2.GetSheHe] throws [combatant_2.GetHerHis]self at you, ignoring your blows, but soon enough you've hacked [combatant_2.GetHerHim] to pieces.

The cheering of the crowd intoxicates you as you strike and kick your opponent on the ground. The duel might end sooner than you thought, [combatant_2.GetFirstName] was easy to disarm and cut down.\n Yet, as you prepare to end [combatant_2.GetHerHis] sufferings, [combatant_2.GetSheHe] rises up suddenly, stopping your blade with [combatant_2.GetHerHis] bare hands and headbutting you. You're almost about to lose grip of your weapon in the commotion, but you manage to hold tight and move forward, making [combatant_2.GetHerHim] impale [combatant_2.GetHerHim]self.

You both lost your weapons during the fight, but that didn't stop you from continuing, grappling and wrestling on the ground.\n [combatant_2.GetFirstName] tries to break your neck, but you pierce [combatant_2.GetHerHis] eye with a nail, breaking [combatant_2.GetHerHis] hold on you. You force [combatant_2.GetHerHim] down, punching repeadetly [combatant_2.GetHerHim] in the head until it's reduced into a bloody pulp.

When [combatant_2.GetFirstName] manages to strike you and draw first blood with a lucky swing, you feel the rage building up inside you. Charging your opponent head-on, you parry [combatant_2.GetHerHis] second strike and trample [combatant_2.GetHerHim]. \n Before [combatant_2.GetSheHe] can get up, you come down on [combatant_2.GetHerHim] starting to bit off pieces of [combatant_2.GetHerHim].\n [combatant_2.GetFirstName] tries to push you back, but it's all for naught and soon you've bled [combatant_2.GetHerHim] dry.

The crowd cheers as you stand over the bloody remains of your defeated opponent, savagely shouting your victory and dedicating the blood tribute to Khorne. Yet, there are more fights to be held, and more challenges for you to be overcome if you wish to truly catch the attention of the Lord of Skulls.
WHO'S NEXT?!

You shout and beat your chest, all covered in steaming blood, surrounded by the dozens of challengers fallen in the quest for glory.\n You never doubted your skill, all this great show of prowess and bloodshed is certain to have endeared Khorne to you. \n The crowd cheers and chants your name, in awe and hidden fear, cowering as you leave the field. Many even start following you, certain that such a strong leader will bring them closer to the Blood God as well.

Your own challenge, your own triumph. You shout and beat your chest, all covered in steaming blood, surrounded by the dozens of challengers fallen in the quest for glory.\n You never doubted your skill, all this great show of prowess and bloodshed is certain to have endeared Khorne to you. \n The crowd cheers and chants your name, in awe and hidden fear, cowering as you leave the field. Many even start following you, certain that such a strong leader will bring them closer to the Blood God as well.
MORE DEATH! MORE BLOOD!!!
[From.GetFirstName] was furious to announce that, due to lack of challengers, the tournament will be cancelled.
All this road for nothing!?!
It's been a long journey, but you're finally back home. A great challenge for Khorne can only be organised every so often. It will be twenty years before another one may be issued...
I'll just kill in some other way!
Khorne favours you! Since you emerged victorious from the ordeal, you can hardly even remember the meaning of fear.
Fear is for cowards and WEAKLINGS!
Surviving the deathmatch made you stronger than you ever were. Khorne must have blessed you!
I'm invincible!
Days have passed since you won the tournament, but it doesn't pass a moment when your mind is not filled with thoughts of blood and violence. The blessing of Khorne filled your heart with rage.
RAAAAAHHHH!!!
You can feel it, more than ever: your victory at the deathmatch did not pass unnoticed in the eyes of the gods. Khorne watches you with approval, new glory awaits you for certain.
BLOOD FOR THE BLOOD GOD!

The Architect of Fate is an unknowable Master. He has taken your offering of blood and trust at the altar of treason, but has repaid you with treason in return. You've killed those that were dear to you, but it'll be all for nothing.
More, I need more sacrifices.

You cut down your friends and family one by one, personally, looking them in the eyes as the treasonous act unravels before them, in their last minute of life. As their blood spills on the altar, drops start flying and flickering beside you and soon an entire army of daemons stands ready at your command.
Power!
What kind of generous gift should you bestow this time upon [From.GetFirstName], so that [From.GetSheHe] may share in Nurgle's magnificence?
The delicate numbing touch of leprosy.
The heart-warming heat of consumption.
The popping joys of the creeping fever.
The great kiss of Nurgle's rot.

You wondered why [From.GetFirstName] was spending so much time with you these past days. Now you know: [From.GetSheHe] was preparing you, unknowing, to receive one of Nurgle's gifts. Dead flesh starts falling off your bones.

You wondered why [From.GetFirstName] was spending so much time with you these past days. Now you know: [From.GetSheHe] was preparing you, unknowing, to receive one of Nurgle's gifts. Blood starts coming out your lungs.

You wondered why [From.GetFirstName] was spending so much time with you these past days. Now you know: [From.GetSheHe] was preparing you, unknowing, to receive one of Nurgle's gifts. Itchy fever-inducing buboes start covering your skin.

You wondered why [From.GetFirstName] was spending so much time with you these past days. Now you know: [From.GetSheHe] was preparing you, unknowing, to receive one of Nurgle's gifts. Your flesh starts rotting and turning into a sickly green hue.
Your entire body is changing shape, strange forms bursting out of your flesh. When you wake, it is clear to you: the Ruinous Powers have bestowed the ultimate gift upon you.
Finally.
Skull-Torc of the Pit
A heavy brass torc strung with the teeth of those who fell in Khorne's blood tournament. The metal is always warm, and on quiet nights it hums for more.
The Everchosen

The End is nigh! Word has come out of the north: a new Everchosen, the anointed champion of all four Ruinous Powers, has risen in the Chaos Wastes, and the tribes of the north are gathering beneath the banner of the eight-pointed star. Whether this Everchosen brings forth the End Times or falls before the stalwart defenders of the world remains to be seen...
[Root.Religion.GetHighGodName], protect us!
FOR CHAOS!
More spiky gitz fer stomping!
Bah, a puppet of the Dark Gods!
Yes-yes, it is time-hour for the Great Ascendancy!
The Everchosen Falls!

Everchosen [Root.GetFirstName] has fallen! Whether by the sword or by treachery, the anointed champion of the Dark Gods is dead, and the great horde is already breaking apart into squabbling warbands. The defenders of Order can rest easy... for now. Chaos has no beginning, and so it has no end.\n\nIn time, another Everchosen will ride out of the Chaos Wastes and once more bring ruin in the name of the Dark Gods.
Victory! Praise the gods!
Weakling! Failure!

[Root.GetTitledFirstName] [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName]! I offer you this one chance to fulfil your destiny and ride with the Host of Chaos Undivided. Kneel, and you will share in the spoils of the world. Refuse, and I will bring you ruin.\n\n[From.GetTitledFirstName], Everchosen of the Dark Gods
Come and get me, coward!
I kneel before the Everchosen.
[From.GetBestName] has spurned your offer and refused [From.GetHerHis] destiny in the service of the Ruinous Powers. [From.GetHerHisCap] suffering will be endless.
I BRING RUIN!
[From.GetBestName] has accepted [From.GetHerHis] destiny and pledged [From.PrimaryTitle.GetName] to the Host of Chaos Undivided. A warbanner of your host now flies over [From.GetHerHis] warriors.
As it should be.
Warbanner of the Everchosen's Host

A tattered standard of flayed hide and blackened iron, bearing the eight-pointed star of Chaos Undivided. The Everchosen sends one to every chieftain who kneels, so that all may know whose host they ride with.

The Everchosen is the champion of all four Chaos Gods, the one mortal behind whom the Ruinous Powers stand united. Far to the north of Naggaroth, beyond the last Druchii watchtowers, the Altar of Ultimate Darkness waits for those who dare to claim the mantle. Many have climbed its steps. Few have come down again.
Lead an army into the province of the Altar of Ultimate Darkness in northern Naggaroth to begin the trials.

You make your way across the wastes, into the northern limits of Naggaroth, where the stories tell of the Altar of Ultimate Darkness. After many trials you reach it at last: a black ziggurat rising out of the ice, its steps slick with the frozen blood of those who came before you.
Ascend the altar and enter the temple!

Upon entering the temple you are beset by nightmarish visions, testing your faith to its very core. Your mind holds, and at last you come to the test: a champion of one of the four gods steps out of the dark. You must defeat [combatant_2.GetHerHim] to earn the mark of the Dark Gods!
I will prove myself worthy - charge!

The body of the first champion has not yet cooled when the shadows stir again. A warrior in black plate, bearing the eight-pointed star of Chaos Undivided, raises [combatant_2.GetHerHis] blade in silent salute. The gods are not yet satisfied.
Deeper in the temple, the walls bleed and whisper. A third champion waits for you here, scarred by a hundred victories and favoured by [combatant_2.GetHerHis] god. One more death, and then another.

At the heart of the temple, before the altar itself, the last champion stands. Four voices whisper in your skull as one, and you understand: this is the final trial. Win, and the world will kneel. Lose, and you will feed the Dark Gods forever.

You have defeated the last champion, and at last you kneel before the Altar of Ultimate Darkness and receive the mark of the Dark Gods. 'Rise... Everchosen... and conquer in our name,' a terrible unison of four voices growls in your head...

The End is nigh! [Root.GetTitledName] has climbed the steps of the Altar of Ultimate Darkness, slain the champions of the four gods and risen as the Everchosen, anointed champion of the Ruinous Powers. Already the tribes of the north are gathering beneath the banner of the eight-pointed star...

You return to your lands bearing the mark of the Gods. Across the wastes the word spreads like wildfire: an Everchosen has been anointed, and the daemons of all four gods march at [Root.GetHerHis] side! The chieftains of the north would be fools not to join you in the war to come...
Let all bow before the Everchosen!

An Everchosen has been anointed at the Altar of Ultimate Darkness. [From.GetTitledName] calls every chieftain of the north to [From.GetHerHis] banner, and daemons of all four gods march with [From.GetHerHim]. Surely you should march to war alongside this new champion?
Yes, I will march alongside the Everchosen!
No, I will never kneel to that fool.

You reach the end of your road only to find the altar cold and silent. Word comes out of the Wastes soon after: the Dark Gods have already anointed another as their Everchosen. Your sacrifices were for nothing, and the gods do not explain themselves.
Curse them all!
Throw a Revel of Excess
Throw open your halls to a revel in honour of the Dark Prince: wine, music, flesh and every other excess your court can devise. Slaanesh may be pleased, but excess has its price.
Has not thrown a Revel of Excess in the last five years

Your stewards have emptied the cellars, your musicians have tuned their strange instruments, and perfumed smoke already hangs beneath the rafters. Guests arrive from across your realm, masked and eager.\n\nOne question remains: how far should the revel go? A lavish feast will please your guests. A revel without limits might please the Dark Prince himself... if anyone survives it.
A lavish feast. Let us not get carried away.
No limits. Nothing is forbidden tonight!

The revel lasts for three days and three nights, and on the last night the music changes. Nobody can say who is playing it. The candles burn violet, the air tastes of honey, and for one breathless moment every guest feels the gaze of the Dark Prince upon them.\n\nSlaanesh is pleased with you.

The revel lasts for three days and three nights, and on the last night the music changes. Nobody can say who is playing it. The candles burn violet, the air tastes of honey, and for one breathless moment every guest feels the gaze of the Dark Prince upon them.\n\nWhen the guests stagger home, one of them stays: a stranger of impossible, unsettling beauty, with eyes like a cat's and claws where hands should be. The Dark Prince has sent you a gift.
The Dark Prince smiles upon me!

On the morning after, your servants find [revel_victim.GetTitledFirstName] lying among the cushions, cold and still, with a smile on [revel_victim.GetHerHis] lips and a goblet still in [revel_victim.GetHerHis] hand.\n\nWine, smoke, flesh, or simply too much of everything: nobody can say what killed [revel_victim.GetHerHim]. Your priests say it was a good death, as deaths go. Slaanesh takes the greatest delight in those who pursue pleasure to its very end.
Died doing what [revel_victim.GetSheHe] loved. A fine way to go.

The revel ends, but not for everyone. Some of your courtiers have found new appetites in the perfumed dark, and they show no sign of giving them up.\n\nYour court is a little louder, a little hungrier and a little more devoted to the Dark Prince than it was before.
As it should be.

The revel was magnificent. Everyone says so. And yet you felt nothing.\n\nThe wine tasted of water, the music was noise, and the flesh was only flesh. This is the curse that Slaanesh lays upon all who chase excess: every pleasure fades, and each new one must be greater than the last. Already you find yourself wondering what it would take to feel something again.
Nothing satisfies me any more...
Pain. Other people's pain. Perhaps that will do.
Not yet.

The Bloodthirster's corpse smokes on the shrine floor, its own whip still knotted around its throat. Be'lakor, the first of the Chosen and the most bitter, lifts the Crown of Domination from the withered king on the throne of corpses and sets it on your brow. The Eye of Sheerian blazes in its socket and for a moment you see every road the world could take, and every one of them ends in fire. The Dark Prince's voice is a hiss of hatred and awe: "Rise, Lord of the End Times." Armour, blade, eye, steed and crown. The six treasures of Necrodomo's prophecy are yours, and the Wastes kneel.

The last champion's heart is still beating when you tear it out and lay it on the black stone. The altar drinks. Darkness swallows the torches and something vast leans close in the dark, four voices speaking as one. Pain sears your brow as the Mark of Chaos burns into your flesh: the sign of all four gods, given to one mortal in an age. No other may walk this road while you live.\n\nWhile you knelt before the gods your warband did not idle. They marched south to the Gulf of Naggarond, fell on the port of Tullich, burned its docks and seized every ship in the harbour. They wait for you there.
To the ships.
You leave your lands behind as Archaon did: your realm becomes a Chaos horde.
Lead your army in person to §YTullich§! (or §YWryn§!) on the Gulf of Naggarond, where your warband holds the captured ships.

Smoke rises over Tullich. A warband bearing the eight-pointed star fell on the port in the night, slaughtered the dockhands, burned the warehouses and sailed off with every ship in the harbour. The survivors speak of a champion marked by all four of the Dark Gods, kneeling at the Altar of Ultimate Darkness while his warriors did his work.
Hunt them down!

Your warband greets you on the burning quays of Tullich with the captured fleet riding at anchor. The largest ship is black iron from keel to mast, and a sea-drake chained to its prow strains against its harness. Across the Sea of Chaos lies the grey isle of Ildelver, where the necropolis of a sunless city hides the armour of Morkar the Uniter, first of the Everchosen.
Set sail for Ildelver.
Embark and sail your army to the isle of §YIldelver§! in the Sea of Chaos, then land there in person.

Ildelver is a grey rock under a sky that never clears. Pale, stooped half-men watch from the mists and flee into holes in the earth when your scouts come near. Somewhere below lies the necropolis where Morkar's armour was laid with his bones, but the isle is a maze of barrows and sea caves.
Search the barrows.
Catch one of the pale things and make it talk.
If the search fails, your army may search again in a month, as long as you stay on the isle.

The barrows split open at dusk. Out of the earth march the dead of the necropolis: pale half-men with blind white eyes, and behind them the barrow-wights of the old Kul in rusted mail, shields still painted with the eight-pointed star. At their head walks a tall shade in a ghost of black armour. Morkar the Uniter, first of the Everchosen, will not give up his armour to a lesser heir. Win the field and his shade dies with his host. Lose it, and you will lie in his barrows forever.
Form the battle line.

The shade of Morkar falls with the last of his dead and his scream fades into the stone. In the deepest tomb the Armour of Morkar waits around a heap of dust, and it closes around you as though it had waited centuries for you. Next is the dragon Flamefang, who guards the Eye of Sheerian at the Cliff of Beasts on the northern coast of Norsca.
It fits as if it were forged for me.
Sail to the northern coast of Norsca and lead your army in person to §YErgren's Peninsula§!, §YDrergen Mort§! or the §YForest of Frykt§!: the Cliff of Beasts.
The Mark is not given to those who wait, and the gods' patience thins. Lead your army in person to Ansar Har in northern Naggaroth, to the Altar of Ultimate Darkness.
Your warband still holds the ships at Tullich, but it will not wait forever. Lead your army in person to Tullich or Wryn on the Gulf of Naggarond.
The Armour of Morkar lies unclaimed in the necropolis. Sail your army to the isle of Ildelver in the Sea of Chaos and land there in person.
Flamefang still sleeps on the Eye of Sheerian. Lead your army in person to the northern coast of Norsca: Ergren's Peninsula, Drergen Mort or the Forest of Frykt.

Two treasures remain. Lead your army in person to the Chimera Plateau, the hobgoblin lands of Khutalai, Avagrom or Dalekland on the Khuuitan Shelf, for the Slayer of Kings. Dorghar waits in the Realm of Chaos once the blade is yours.
Every treasure but the crown is yours. Lead your army in person to Zanbaijin on the Plateau of K'Datha, where Be'lakor waits.
I go.

The Cliff of Beasts is a wall of black rock above a grey sea, and its caves stink of sulphur and old bones. The dragon Flamefang uncoils from its hoard and the Eye of Sheerian glitters among the gold. It does not speak. It opens its jaws, and the world goes dark and hot as it swallows you whole.
Cut my way out.

You climb out of the dragon's belly through its ribs, black with its blood, the Armour of Morkar smoking but whole. The Eye of Sheerian is yours: a stone that shows what is to come. Two treasures remain, and the order is yours to choose: Dorghar, the Steed of the Apocalypse, in the menagerie of the Daemon Prince Agrammon in the Realm of Chaos, or the Slayer of Kings, buried in the chest of Krakanrok the Black on the Chimera Plateau.
Into the Realm of Chaos for the steed.
East, to the Chimera Plateau.
You set out on a pilgrimage into the Realm of Chaos. No army can follow you there.
Lead your army in person to the Chimera Plateau: §YKhutalai§!, §YAvagrom§! or §YDalekland§! on the Khuuitan Shelf.
The world thins and tears, and you step through into the Realm of Chaos. Here the land is thought made flesh, and each of the four gods holds a road to Agrammon's menagerie. You must choose one.
The brass road of Khorne, paved with skulls.
The shifting labyrinth of Tzeentch.
The rotting garden of Nurgle.
The scented palace of Slaanesh.
Your mind frays.

Agrammon's menagerie spreads over miles of cages and pits, holding beasts from every corner of the Realm of Chaos. Daemon keepers prowl between them with hooks and whips. Somewhere inside is the steed you came for.
Cut through the keepers.
Slip past them in the dark.
Hide beneath a beast and track the steed by its stench.
If you fail, you may try again in a month.
You find it at last: a horse, then a wolf, then a thing of scales and eyes, never the same shape twice. As you seize its mane it bursts into flame and bucks to throw you into the fire.
Hold on, whatever it becomes.

The flames die to embers and the beast stands still under you, a black warhorse with burning eyes. Dorghar, the Steed of the Apocalypse, is broken to your will. You ride out of the Realm of Chaos before Agrammon learns what he has lost.
Ride.
Lead your army in person to §YZanbaijin§! on the Plateau of K'Datha, where Be'lakor waits with the Crown of Domination.

Krakanrok the Black, father of the Dragon Ogres, sleeps on the Chimera Plateau like a mountain of scales, and the hilt of a great sword juts from his chest. You draw it while he sleeps. The daemon U'zuhl, bound inside the blade, shrieks loud enough to shake the plateau, and the great chest beneath you begins to rise. The Slayer of Kings must drink before Krakanrok wakes. Royal blood will silence it with one death. Lesser blood will take everyone who came with you.
Quench it in the blood of [blood_offering.GetTitledFirstName].
There is no royal blood here. Give it all of them.
I came alone...
The blade drinks and U'zuhl falls silent, for now. Its hunger will return. The Slayer of Kings is yours.
To Zanbaijin.
Into the Realm of Chaos for the steed.

Zanbaijin rises from the Plateau of K'Datha, the greatest city of the Wastes, built on bones older than the Empire. The city opens its gates to the Mark on your brow and the treasures you carry: it is yours, the seat from which you will rule the end of the world. In the shadow of its walls a figure of living darkness waits for you.
This is my throne.

Be'lakor, the first of the Chosen, cursed by Tzeentch never to rule, leads you to the shrine where the crown waits. "Every Everchosen must pass the gods' tests," he hisses, "and I must crown every one of them." Plague comes first, then a maze of crystal that shows you everything except the way out, then a perfumed voice offering you everything you have ever wanted. Khorne's test waits at the end.
Walk blind through the maze and trust the gods.
Read the maze with my own eyes.

The crown sits on a withered corpse on a throne at the heart of the shrine. Between you and it stands a Bloodthirster of Khorne, axe in one hand and whip in the other. It has waited a thousand years to kill whoever comes for the crown.
Take its whip and strangle it with it.
No other seeker holds the Mark of Chaos.
Seeker of the Mark
Lead your army in person to Ansar Har in northern Naggaroth, to the Altar of Ultimate Darkness.
Marked by Chaos: to the Ships
Lead your army in person to Tullich or Wryn on the Gulf of Naggarond, where your warband holds the captured ships.
Marked by Chaos: the Armour of Morkar
Sail your army to the isle of Ildelver in the Sea of Chaos and land there in person.
Marked by Chaos: the Eye of Sheerian
Lead your army in person to the northern coast of Norsca: Ergren's Peninsula, Drergen Mort or the Forest of Frykt.
Marked by Chaos: the Steed and the Blade
The Slayer of Kings: lead your army in person to Khutalai, Avagrom or Dalekland on the Khuuitan Shelf. Dorghar: a pilgrimage into the Realm of Chaos, offered when the Eye or the blade is won.
Marked by Chaos: the Crown of Domination
Lead your army in person to Zanbaijin on the Plateau of K'Datha.
Ships Seized by Chaos
A marked champion's warband burned the docks and stole every ship in the harbour.

Your line breaks. The dead do not tire and do not flee, and their cold hands drag your warriors down into the barrows one by one. The shade of Morkar finds you in the mud and the dark. 'Not you,' he whispers. 'Never you.'
No...
The host of the dead rises on Ildelver and attacks your army at once. If you win the battle, the shade of Morkar dies and the armour is yours. If you lose, you die among the barrows.
Everyone who stands with you on the plateau dies.
The Dark Gods will not let you die here: you are thrown aside, wounded, and may try again.
The Winds of Chaos blow at their strongest.
Host of the Necropolis
Shade
Khorne
Nurgle
Slaanesh
Tzeentch
the Chaos Gods
the Blood God
Grandfather Nurgle
the Dark Prince
the Changer of Ways
the Four Powers
the Brass Citadel
the Garden of Nurgle
the Palace of Pleasure
the Crystal Labyrinth

Champion

Voice of Khorne
The Blood God growls in this warrior's skull, naming the next foe whose skull is owed to the Skull Throne.
Voice of Nurgle
Grandfather Nurgle murmurs fondly in this servant's ear, counting the blessings of rot that are yet to come.
Voice of Slaanesh
The Dark Prince whispers sweet promises to this servant, and every word drips with honeyed want.
Voice of Tzeentch
A thousand voices of the Changer of Ways chatter in this servant's mind. Some of them even tell the truth.
Voice of the Dark Gods
The Four Powers speak to this servant as one, and for once they do not quarrel.

The dream comes on the night of a black moon. You stand alone on a plain of ash, and the sky above you is an eye. It is the Eye of the Gods, and it has found you wanting.\n\nThere is no rage in the gaze of [Root.GetPatronTitle], only contempt. Then it turns away, and as it leaves you, so does the glory of a [Root.GetPatronRank]. You wake cold. Your followers already whisper that [Root.GetPatronGod] has cast you down.

You wake screaming, the stink of burnt flesh in your nose. The mark of [Root.GetPatronGod] that you bore so proudly is gone, seared off your skin by a fire that left no other burn.\n\nThe judgement of [Root.GetPatronTitle] is final: nothing in you is worth keeping. Your warband looks at the raw scar and says nothing. Nobody needs to.

It strikes you in the middle of the feast. One moment you are laughing at a rival's ruin, the next you are on the flagstones while something unseen tears at you with claws of warp-stuff.\n\nWhen your guards drag you clear, you are a ruin yourself. You live, for now, by the mercy of [Root.GetPatronTitle], so that every servant of [Root.GetPatronGod] who sees your broken body remembers the price of failure.

You have failed [Root.GetPatronGod] for the last time. The air of your hall splits like rotten cloth, and beyond it lies [Root.GetPatronRealm]. Something reaches through.\n\nYour court will never agree on what they saw. Some say a great hand, some say a burning mouth. All agree that when the rift closed, you were gone, and the screaming went on for a long time after.

The changes come all at once. Bones crack and lengthen, skin splits to show new mouths, eyes bloom where no eyes should be. The protection of [Root.GetPatronTitle] has been withdrawn, leaving you naked to the raw stuff of Chaos, and your body has given up all pretence of being a body.\n\nWhen it is over, there is no lord in your hall, only a gibbering, mewling heap of flesh that was once a [Root.GetPatronRank] of [Root.GetPatronGod]. Your heirs drive it out into the wilds with spears.
Fallen... but not finished.
I will earn it again, in blood if I must.
Even in ruin, I serve.
No... NO!
Gnnnhhhaaa...

The omens are bad, and everyone can read them. A two-headed calf in the stables, a comet that burns the wrong colour, a prophet in the market who screams your name and then bites off his own tongue.\n\nYou have earned the displeasure of [Root.GetPatronGod], and the whole realm knows it. Your rivals smile behind their hands.

For a season, your prayers fall into silence. The altar fires gutter, the sacrifices spoil before the knife touches them, and your priests mutter that your prayers no longer reach [Root.GetPatronTitle].\n\nYou have chased mortal glory too hard, and neglected the god who gave you your strength.

You are riding out when your horse screams and throws you. As you fall you glimpse something in the long grass, a thing from [Root.GetPatronRealm] that should not be here, and then it is on you.\n\nIt does not kill you. It only marks you, carefully and cruelly, before it fades. A reminder from [Root.GetPatronTitle] not to grow arrogant.

The servants of [Root.GetPatronGod] who answer your summonings come slower now, and sneer as they kneel. Even the lesser daemons can smell it on you: the interest of [Root.GetPatronTitle] in you has cooled.\n\nWhether it is a failing, too much success or simple whim, only the Dark Gods know. But the favour you have built up drains away like blood from a wound.
I will bear it.
Spill blood and gold on the altar until the gods relent.

A daemon comes to you in your sleep and sits upon your chest, and it talks to you all night of what is wanted from a [Root.GetPatronRank] of [Root.GetPatronGod]. You cannot remember a word of it in the morning.\n\nBut you are not quite the same as you were. Something in your temper has been turned, gently, like a key in a lock.

You wake to find your bedsheets soaked and your body changed. The touch of [Root.GetPatronGod] has reshaped your flesh in the night.\n\nIs it a blessing or a warning? With the Dark Gods it is often both. Your servants avoid your eyes while they dress you.

Word spreads among the warbands that the eye of [Root.GetPatronGod] has rested upon you, and that you did not flinch. Lesser men come to look upon you, hoping that some of that glory will rub off on them.\n\nFrom [Root.GetPatronTitle] there is no further word. But the mortals have noticed, and that is a start.

For three nights the altar fires burn without fuel, and in the smoke your priests see your name written in the script of [Root.GetPatronRealm].\n\nIt is a small sign. A god's nod across a crowded room. But your faithful take heart.

You feel the Eye of the Gods upon you, heavy as a hand on the back of the neck. You wait for wrath, or for glory.\n\nNothing comes. The Eye has looked, and weighed, and moved on, and you are left with silence. Not disapproval, not reward. Merely nothing.
I am remade in my master's image.
My flesh is clay in my master's hands.
Let them look.
A sign! I am watched over.
Then I will do something they cannot ignore.

You rise from your bed and the bed groans. Your arms are thicker, your back is straighter, and when you grip your sword the hilt cracks.\n\nIn reward for your service, your body has been judged unfit for a [Root.GetPatronRank] of [Root.GetPatronGod], and improved.

At the height of the rite, the altar flames turn the colour of [Root.GetPatronRealm] and form a crown above your head. Every priest in the temple falls to their knees.\n\nYou have been proclaimed a true believer of [Root.GetPatronGod] and a paragon among the faithful, though not yet a favourite.

Your victories are sung in every warcamp from the Chaos Wastes to the Old World. Heralds of other lords come to your hall with gifts, and warriors come seeking a place under your banner.\n\nThe gods remain aloof, as gods do. But your fame has grown, and with it the glory of [Root.GetPatronGod].

Your old wounds close in the night. Grey hairs darken again. When the physician comes, he finds the heartbeat of a much younger [Root.GetManWoman].\n\nFor your great service, your life has been lengthened by [Root.GetPatronTitle], so that you may toil longer in the name of [Root.GetPatronGod].

It begins as a murmur at the edge of hearing, when you are alone. Then it is a whisper. Then it is a voice, and you know whose voice it is.\n\nIt is [Root.GetPatronTitle], speaking in your mind of the paths to greater favour. You will never be alone again.

A gift of [Root.GetPatronGod] settles over you like a cloak. You feel it in the set of your shoulders, the line of your jaw, the speed of your thoughts.\n\nYou have been made more fitting to stand at the forefront of the servants of [Root.GetPatronTitle], and everyone can see it.

For a year and a day, a herald of [Root.GetPatronRealm] attends you, unseen by all but you. It teaches you how the truly great servants of [Root.GetPatronGod] live: how they fight, how they rule, how they spend their idle hours.\n\nWhen it leaves, your old habits are gone, and new ones have taken their place.

The Winds of Magic have always blown past you. Now they blow through you. You see them, taste them, feel them twist around your fingers like eager hounds.\n\nThe touch of [Root.GetPatronGod] has woken the sorcery in your blood. Use it well, or it will use you.
Stronger. Always stronger.
I am the faithful sword of [Root.GetPatronGod].
Let the world know my name!
More years to spend in my master's service.
Speak, my lord. I am listening.
I wear my master's gift with pride.
I will live as my master wills.
Power! At last, true power!

The Eye of the Gods opens above your hall, and this time it does not look away. A voice like the end of the world speaks your name, and the mark of [Root.GetPatronGod] on your skin blazes until your court must shield their eyes.\n\nIn recognition of your skill and devotion, you have been named one of the Champions of [Root.GetPatronGod]. It is not the greatest honour the Dark Gods give, but it sets you apart from the countless thousands who crave their attention.

When you wake there is something lying at the foot of your bed that was not there when you lay down. It is warm to the touch, and it hums faintly with the power of [Root.GetPatronRealm].\n\nThrough your toil and slaughter you have once again caught the eye of your lord. A gift worthy of a [Root.GetPatronRank] has come from [Root.GetPatronTitle], and the whole realm knows it.
For [Root.GetPatronGod]!
My lord is generous.
The Raven's Child

The Raven came to me in the night. Its feathers shimmered with every colour and none, and its voice was a thousand voices.\n\nIt told me to take up arms, gather the faithful and be their prophet. It told me to march south, to Kislev, and tear the land of the ice witches from the grasp of weak men and their dead gods. It told me the Wastes themselves would open a road for me.
I must go at once!
The Death of [From.GetFirstName]

I have rid the world of [From.GetFirstName], and with [From.GetHerHim] the mad dream of a Black Crusade led by a child. The children and the wretches who flocked to [From.GetHerHis] banner have scattered to the four winds, wailing that the Raven has abandoned them.\n\nPerhaps it has. Or perhaps the Changer of Ways wanted exactly this.

I feared my [GetFromRelation]'s zeal for the Raven God would lead [From.GetHerHim] to an early grave, and so it has. [From.GetFirstName] is gone. The children and wretches who followed [From.GetHerHim] have scattered to the four winds, unable to understand why [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] would let their prophet die with [From.GetHerHis] task undone.\n\nThe Changer of Ways weaves many threads. It seems [From.GetFirstName] was no longer one of them.

[From.GetFirstName] is dead, and with [From.GetHerHim] the dream of a Black Crusade led by a child. The children and wretches who followed [From.GetHerHim] have scattered to the four winds, unable to understand why [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] would let their prophet die with [From.GetHerHis] task undone.\n\nThe Changer of Ways weaves many threads. It seems [From.GetFirstName] was no longer one of them.
Such a short thread, for such a young [From.GetBoyGirl].

[From.GetFirstName] sits in my dungeon, and the Raven's Child is a prophet no more. [From.GetHerHis] followers are already drifting away, muttering that [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] would never let [From.GetHerHis] chosen one be caught so easily.
[From.GetSheHeCap] will stay there until [From.GetSheHe] learns some sense.

[FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has taken [From.GetFirstName] prisoner, and the Raven's Child will lead no one to Kislev. [From.GetHerHis] followers have scattered, wailing that [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] would never let [From.GetHerHis] chosen one fall so easily.\n\nThe Changer of Ways weaves many threads. It seems [From.GetFirstName] was no longer one of them.
Perhaps it is for the best.
The Chosen Child

Something has happened to my [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName].

[From.GetSheHeCap] swears the Raven came to [From.GetHerHim] in the night and ordered [From.GetHerHim] to gather the true faithful, become their prophet and lead a Black Crusade against the weak men of Kislev. [From.GetHerHis] eyes have changed colour since. Twice.

Now [From.GetSheHe] demands money, weapons and warriors to show my faith in [From.GetHerHis] holy task, and will not hear a word of reason. [From.GetSheHeCap] means to leave [Root.Capital.GetName] at once.

[From.GetFirstName], a child of [Root.Capital.GetName], has caused quite a stir. [From.GetSheHeCap] forced [From.GetHerHis] way into my hall and announced that the Raven came to [From.GetHerHim] in a dream and ordered [From.GetHerHim] to gather the true faithful of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] and lead a Black Crusade against Kislev.\n\nThe brat finished [From.GetHerHis] sermon by ordering me to provide money, weapons and warriors, in the name of the Changer of Ways.
You will have my full support!
I will send some warriors to guard you.
Take some food for the road.
Of course! I will even find you a boat south.
You are dead to me. Go, and never come back!
Guards! Throw this babbling fool out!
If this is what you want, I will not stop you.
Do as you like. It is no concern of mine.

Word comes from [FromFrom.Capital.GetName] of a [FromFrom.GetBoyGirl] who has dreamed of the Raven. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] has proclaimed [FromFrom.GetHerselfHimself] the prophet of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] and called the true faithful to a Black Crusade against the weak men of Kislev.\n\nThousands of runaway children, outcasts and starving wretches already follow [FromFrom.GetHerHim] across the Wastes. [FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] says the Wastes themselves will open a road to the south.
A wild imagination, even for a child.
May [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] show [childrens_crusade_leader.GetHerHim] the road to victory!
Could this child truly speak for the Changer of Ways?

The ragged host of [childrens_crusade_leader.GetFirstName] has reached [Root.Capital.GetName]: a parade of shrieking children, cripples and starvelings that has already stripped the fields bare. As if that were not enough, their small prophet has demanded an audience and informs me that I am to feed and shelter [childrens_crusade_leader.GetHerHis] holy warriors.
Your cause has moved me! I will support you.
Take some supplies and go.
